claims.title: Two auxiliary unipotent levels make the actual stabilizers trivial
claims.statement: The definite integral lattice makes every rational level-class stabilizer finite. At two distinct auxiliary rational primes, the literal iwU conditions force its order to be a power of each prime; hence it is trivial. This also proves freeness of the actual local lattice-tuple action and C.StabZero.

The literal local package uses the same host, p, orbit positions, coefficient extension and LocId as the source. LI1--LI7 supply those identifications under their stated hypotheses.
The integral Weyl lattice Delta is not identified with the dual-Weyl coefficient lattice nabla. CB2--CB3 and IW3 are used for rational dimension only.

The auxiliary primes are distinct and prime, as supplied by D.host.g_prime and D.host.g_ne. Their actual level is the inverse image of the upper-unitriangular residue subgroup, not necessarily a principal congruence kernel.
claims.source_relation: Minkowski boundedness gives the same finite-stabilizer result as the source's trace-denominator construction. The prime-to-g torsion proof uses separated congruence induction, preserving the actual iwU condition even for g=2.
